correctness.rationale: PASS: Write A=π(n²), h=π((n+1)²)−π(n²). For n≥100 every prime in the interval is coprime to six, hence h≤2 floor((2n+1)/6)+2≤(2n+7)/3. Rosser–Schoenfeld π(n²)>n²/(2log n) yields n log(1+h/A)<(4/3+14/(3n))log n≤1.38log n, while log A>2log n−log(2log n)>1.5log n for n≥100. Thus A^(n+1)>(A+h)^n. Independently sieved/trial-checked every integer through 10000 and verified all 97 exact integer-power inequalities for n=3..99; n=2 fails. Finite range is genuinely exhaustive and tail proven analytically.
